own_solution.law: Calorimetry energy balance: m_w c (dT0 - T) = m_i L + m_i c T, with T measured above the melting point; heat given up Q = m_w c (dT0 - T)
assumptions: insulated, no heat to container or surroundings
all ice melts (checked: 83.7 kJ available > 26.7 kJ needed)
constant c and L, no evaporation

defect_reasons.other: In T96AB 'the water' is not tied to a container while the scene has warm water in two containers; context (the ice is added to the first) makes the first the natural reading.

notes: Base: 0.5*4186*(40 - T) = 0.08*334000 + 0.08*4186*T gives 57000 = 2427.88 T, T = 23.477 K above melting; Q = 2093*(40 - 23.477) = 34582 J. With 17 K heating (57 K): 92581 = 2427.88 T, T = 38.132 K; Q = 26720 + 334.88*38.132 = 39490 J. 'Starts 40 K above' refers to the temperature when poured, before anything is done, so a later heating before the ice is added is consistent. Second-container heating (TA38E, T162D) and earlier-run heating (T2F5B, T32CB) are disconnected. T2F5B and T162D state no number ('a small amount').
